name: Greg Penner

views.text: Dead money is a cost, not a reason to keep a quarterback who is not the answer.
I hired a coach to make football decisions, and I back them.
Every choice is a bet on winning more games, not on protecting the books.
A rookie quarterback with the right coach is worth a patient year.
We built the facilities and the staff to compete with anyone.
A playoff return is the minimum; titles are the point.

signatures: frames hard money decisions as bets on winning
defers football questions to his head coach
want: Bring a fourth championship to Denver under the ownership group he leads (medium).
voice: Calm, analytical and corporate; talks in terms of investment and outcomes. Rarely emotional in public and comfortable letting his coach be the face of the team.

evidence.summary: Denver released Russell Wilson and absorbed a then-record $85 million in dead money.
Penner said the financial fallout of moving on from Wilson would not decide the quarterback question and framed it as a bet on winning, backing Sean Payton's call.

review.notes: Thin coverage: two to four sources found by web search (2026-11-06); sliders mostly left at 5; a few publication dates are taken from the news cycle the article covers. Draft for JR to check.
